title: Apply formulas to both terms
text: Apply the power-reducing formulas to both squared terms: $$\sin**2(x)=\frac{1-\cos(2x)}{2}$$ and $$\cos**2(x)=\frac{1+\cos(2x)}{2}.$$

title: Multiply the fractions
text: Multiply the two fractions together: $$\left(\frac{1-\cos(2x)}{2}\right)\left(\frac{1+\cos(2x)}{2}\right).$$ Notice the numerator is a difference of squares.

title: Expand the numerator
text: Expanding yields $$\frac{1-\cos**2(2x)}{4}.$$ We still have a squared trigonometric term, so we must apply the power-reducing formula again to $$\cos**2(2x).$$

title: Second power reduction
text: Applying the formula to $$2x$$ yields $$\cos**2(2x)=\frac{1+\cos(4x)}{2}.$$ Substitute this back in: $$\frac{1-\left(\frac{1+\cos(4x)}{2}\right)}{4}.$$

title: Simplify the complex fraction
text: Multiply the top and bottom of the main fraction by $$2$$ to clear the nested denominator: $$\frac{2-(1+\cos(4x))}{8}.$$

title: Final Expression
text: Distribute the negative and combine like terms to get the equivalent expression: $$\frac{1-\cos(4x)}{8}.$$
